title: Build a reusable AI workflow for weekly reports
goal: You will create a reusable ChatGPT Project that accepts the same weekly data shape and produces a consistent status report.
prerequisites: A ChatGPT account with access to Projects
One recent week of status notes to test the workflow

steps.action: Create a new Project named "Weekly Status Report."
steps.where: Left sidebar, "New project" button beside the Projects heading.
steps.why: A dedicated Project keeps the reusable instructions and weekly report chats together.
steps.checkpoint: You should see "Weekly Status Report" as the selected Project in the sidebar.
hint_levels: Look in the sidebar under Projects.
Use the New project control, then enter a descriptive project name.
Click New project, type "Weekly Status Report," and click Create project.

steps.where: Project header, three-dot menu beside "Weekly Status Report," then "Project instructions."
steps.why: Project instructions act as the saved prompt that applies to every weekly chat.
steps.checkpoint: You should see an instructions text box for the Weekly Status Report Project.
hint_levels: Look for the menu beside the Project name.
The Project menu contains the reusable instructions setting.
Click the three dots beside Weekly Status Report, then click Project instructions.

steps.action: Enter instructions that define the report sections, writing rules, and handling of missing information.
steps.where: Project instructions text box in the Project instructions dialog.
steps.why: Explicit rules make reports consistent even when the weekly details change.
steps.checkpoint: The editor should visibly include the section names "Summary," "Completed," "In Progress," "Blockers," and "Next Week."
hint_levels: Define both the headings and the tone.
Tell ChatGPT to use those five headings, concise bullets, factual language, and "None reported" when a section lacks data.

Enter: "Create a weekly status report using exactly these headings: Summary, Completed, In Progress, Blockers, Next Week. Write Summary as 2-3 sentences and all other sections as concise bullets. Preserve names, dates, numbers, and links. Do not invent facts. Write 'None reported' when a section has no data."

steps.action: Add a fixed weekly input template beneath the report instructions.
steps.where: Same Project instructions text box, below the output-format rules.
steps.why: A stable input shape makes weekly collection faster and reduces omissions.
steps.checkpoint: You should see labeled fields for reporting period, audience, completed work, work in progress, blockers, next-week priorities, and metrics.
hint_levels: Give each recurring data category its own label.
Add a copyable block with the same seven labels in the same order every week.

Append: "Expect input in this exact shape:
REPORTING PERIOD:
AUDIENCE:
COMPLETED:
IN PROGRESS:
BLOCKERS:
NEXT-WEEK PRIORITIES:
METRICS OR LINKS:"

steps.action: Add a final instruction requiring ChatGPT to flag missing fields before drafting.
steps.where: Bottom of the Project instructions text box.
steps.why: A completeness check prevents polished reports built from incomplete notes.
steps.checkpoint: The last instruction should say to identify missing required fields before producing the report.
hint_levels: Add a quality gate after the template.
Require a short missing-fields list instead of a draft whenever required input is absent.
Append: "Before drafting, check every field; if required information is missing, list the missing fields and wait for my reply."

steps.where: Bottom-right "Save" button in the Project instructions dialog.
steps.why: Saving makes the workflow automatically available in every chat inside this Project.
steps.checkpoint: The instructions dialog should close and the Weekly Status Report Project should remain selected.
hint_levels: Finish the editor before testing.
Use the confirmation button at the bottom of the dialog.
Click Save in the bottom-right corner.

steps.action: Start a new chat inside the Project and paste one week of notes using every input-template label.
steps.where: "New chat" button within the Weekly Status Report Project, then the message composer at the bottom of the chat.
steps.why: A realistic test reveals whether the saved prompt works with the data shape you will reuse.
steps.checkpoint: The composer should show all seven labels populated or explicitly marked "None."
hint_levels: Use the saved field order instead of free-form notes.
Fill each label with this week's facts and write None for empty categories.
Click New chat inside Weekly Status Report, paste the seven-label block, fill it in, then press Enter.

steps.action: Check the generated report against the required headings and source facts.
steps.where: Assistant response in the main chat pane.
steps.why: Verification catches formatting drift and invented or altered details before reuse.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the five headings in the required order, with names, dates, metrics, and links matching your pasted notes.
hint_levels: Compare the response with both the saved format and your input.
Confirm heading order, concise bullets, factual accuracy, and use of None reported where needed.
Read Summary, Completed, In Progress, Blockers, and Next Week in order, then compare every specific fact with the input message above.

steps.action: Rename the test chat with its reporting period.
steps.where: Left sidebar, three-dot menu beside the current chat, then "Rename."
steps.why: Period-based names make past reports easy to locate and provide a repeatable weekly filing convention.
steps.checkpoint: The sidebar should show a chat name such as "Status Report — Aug 3–7, 2026" inside the Project.
hint_levels: Use the report period as the filing key.
Apply the same "Status Report — [period]" naming pattern each week.
In the sidebar, click the chat's three dots, click Rename, enter "Status Report — [reporting period]," and press Enter.
